summary.text: CSUTLDTC is a called date-validation subprogram (no CICS or file I/O) that wraps the Language Environment callable service CEEDAYS. It receives a 10-byte date string, a 10-byte format mask (callers pass 'YYYY-MM-DD') and an 80-byte result area, converts the date and mask into the variable-length strings CEEDAYS expects and calls CEEDAYS to obtain a Lilian day number. It then returns in the result area the CEEDAYS severity (4 digits), the message number (4 digits) and a 15-character text such as 'Date is valid', 'Datevalue error' or 'Invalid month', plus the tested date and mask, and sets RETURN-CODE to the severity. The Lilian date itself is not returned. It is called by CORPT00C and COTRN02C, and the copybook CSUTLDPY also contains a CALL 'CSUTLDTC'.

paragraphs.name: (PROCEDURE DIVISION entry)
paragraphs.logic: Entry point with USING LS-DATE, LS-DATE-FORMAT, LS-RESULT. Initializes WS-MESSAGE, clears WS-DATE, performs A000-MAIN, then moves the 80-byte WS-MESSAGE to LS-RESULT, moves WS-SEVERITY-N to RETURN-CODE and returns with EXIT PROGRAM.

paragraphs.name: A000-MAIN
paragraphs.logic: Builds the CEEDAYS variable-length inputs (length 10 plus text) from LS-DATE and LS-DATE-FORMAT, calls CEEDAYS with OUTPUT-LILLIAN and FEEDBACK-CODE, stores the feedback severity and message number in WS-SEVERITY-N/WS-MSG-NO-N, and maps the feedback token to a 15-character WS-RESULT text ('Date is valid', 'Insufficient', 'Datevalue error', 'Invalid Era', 'Unsupp. Range', 'Invalid month', 'Bad Pic String', 'Nonnumeric data', 'YearInEra is 0', else 'Date is invalid').

paragraphs.name: A000-MAIN-EXIT
paragraphs.logic: Exit paragraph for A000-MAIN; contains only EXIT.

rules.statement: A date is valid when the Language Environment service CEEDAYS can convert the supplied date string using the supplied format mask into a Lilian day number; the validity is expressed by the CEEDAYS feedback severity and message number.
rules.anchor: CALL "CEEDAYS" USING WS-DATE-TO-TEST, WS-DATE-FORMAT, OUTPUT-LILLIAN, FEEDBACK-CODE
rules.outcome: WS-SEVERITY-N and WS-MSG-NO-N set from FEEDBACK-CODE

rules.statement: The CEEDAYS feedback token is translated into a short result text: all-zero token -> 'Date is valid'; message 2507 -> 'Insufficient'; 2508 -> 'Datevalue error'; 2509 -> 'Invalid Era'; 2513 -> 'Unsupp. Range'; 2517 -> 'Invalid month'; 2518 -> 'Bad Pic String'; 2520 -> 'Nonnumeric data'; 2521 -> 'YearInEra is 0'; any other token -> 'Date is invalid'.
rules.anchor: WHEN FC-UNSUPP-RANGE MOVE 'Unsupp. Range ' TO WS-RESULT

rules.statement: The validation outcome is returned to the caller as an 80-byte result (severity in bytes 1-4, 'Mesg Code:', message number in bytes 16-19, result text, tested date and mask) and the CEEDAYS severity is also placed in RETURN-CODE; the subprogram never abends on an invalid date, leaving the decision to the caller.

observations.text: The 88-level named FC-INVALID-DATE has the all-zero feedback value, which means success, and its branch sets 'Date is valid'; the name is misleading.

After the call, the whole WS-DATE-TO-TEST group (2-byte binary length followed by the text) is moved to WS-DATE PIC X(10), overwriting the date moved at 107; the 'TstDate:' part of the result therefore starts with the binary length bytes and loses the last two date characters (Inferred from 25-31, 52 and 122).
The Lilian day number OUTPUT-LILLIAN produced by CEEDAYS is discarded; callers only receive validity information.
Message numbers in the 88-level feedback tokens are encoded in hex (X'09CB'=2507 ... X'09D9'=2521, severity 3, facility 'CEE'); only these nine conditions get specific texts.
DISPLAY WS-MESSAGE and GOBACK are commented out; the program ends with EXIT PROGRAM.

sme_questions.question: Callers CORPT00C and COTRN02C accept message 2513 ('Unsupp. Range') as valid. Is this tolerance intentional, and what date range should actually be accepted?
